classification_basis: Both resolved entrance channels add H across the propene C=C bond to form propyl radicals. This intermolecular alkene-addition family is physically distinct from the frozen intramolecular 5-hexenyl-radical cyclization family.

theory_source.title: Hierarchical Study of the Reactions of Hydrogen Atoms with Alkenes: A Theoretical Study of the Reactions of Hydrogen Atoms with C2-C4 Alkenes
theory_source.method_context: For the C2 and C3 reaction systems the source reports ROCCSD(T)/aug-cc-pVXZ (X=T,Q) single-point calculations extrapolated to the complete-basis-set limit after T1-diagnostic checks; the propene comparison figure labels the current-work addition curves ROCCSD(T)/aug-cc-pVXZ.

barrier_profile.type: source-reported computed activation enthalpy at 0 K, Delta-dagger H_0K
source-reported computed activation enthalpy at 0 K, Delta-dagger H_0K

theory_source.typing_firewall: The 15.61 and 8.39 kJ/mol values remain Delta-dagger H_0K quantities. They are not relabeled as 298 K activation free energies, as the finite-temperature modified-Arrhenius Ea parameters in Table 6, or as experimental activation quantities.
theory_source.high_pressure_rate_model_context: The source separately calculates high-pressure limiting and pressure-dependent rates with RRKM/master-equation methods. Those calculated rates are not substituted for the independent experimental comparator and are not used to select this candidate.

basis: The stated aim is a hierarchical C2-C5 alkene dataset computed at consistent levels of theory rather than a reaction-by-reaction residual-minimization exercise.
The C2/C3 ROCCSD(T) refinement is tied to T1-diagnostic/electronic-structure considerations and computational feasibility.
The source explicitly distinguishes its current-work propene barriers from an older Miller-Klippenstein treatment whose barriers had been altered to improve agreement with experiment.

Only the source's current-work R3/R4 ab initio Delta-dagger H_0K values are retained here. Older empirically altered barriers and the source's later averaged/recommended rate constants are excluded from the validation chain.
Kurylo et al. appears as an experimental comparison in the propene rate figure, but the source does not disclose adjustment of the current-work R3/R4 barrier values to that dataset.

source.title: Temperature and Pressure Effects in the Addition of H Atoms to Propylene

experimental_comparator.technique: hydrogen-atom resonance fluorescence using Lyman-alpha radiation with a helium-pressure series
experimental_comparator.observable: experimentally extrapolated limiting high-pressure second-order total addition rate for H + C3H6 -> C3H7
experimental_comparator.quantity_typing: observed high-pressure limiting rate inferred from the experimental pressure series; not a theoretical rate and not a rate-derived activation barrier
experimental_comparator.temperature_series_context: The same study also measured temperature dependence at 50 Torr from 177 to 473 K. That finite-pressure Arrhenius analysis is not the selected comparator for this trail.

condition_mapping.reaction_identity: H + C3H6 addition on both theory and experiment sides
condition_mapping.temperature: The observed comparator is at 298 K. The theoretical quantities remain explicitly typed 0 K activation enthalpies; no false 298 K free-energy relabeling is made.
condition_mapping.pressure_regime: The observed comparator is the limiting high-pressure rate obtained from an experimental pressure series. The theory explicitly supplies the corresponding high-pressure-limit reaction network as well as pressure-dependent kinetics.
condition_mapping.bath_gas: Helium is part of the experimental pressure-series protocol, but the selected observable is the extrapolated high-pressure limit rather than one finite-He-pressure rate.
condition_mapping.standard_state_units: The observed bimolecular rate remains in cm^3 molecule^-1 s^-1; no solution-standard-state conversion is applied.

independence_basis: The physical family is intermolecular H-atom addition to propene, not another temperature point, isotopologue, or method replicate of the frozen 5-hexenyl cyclization family.

The 1971 kinetic measurement predates the 2021 theory, so chronology alone cannot establish independence; independence instead rests on the source's a-priori electronic-structure protocol and the absence of disclosed fitting of the current-work R3/R4 ab initio barriers to Kurylo's rate.
The source explicitly identifies experiment-adjusted barriers in an older literature model, and those adjusted values are excluded here.
No residual, chi, or expected ChemSA agreement was calculated or used to choose the propene trail or either barrier channel.
representation_basis: The selected experimental k_infinity is for total C3H7 formation and does not resolve n-C3H7 versus i-C3H7 as one scalar elementary channel.
The theory resolves two parallel addition entrance channels with distinct barriers, 15.61 and 8.39 kJ/mol, so both are retained in the barrier profile.
A single-barrier coordinate using only the lower 8.39 kJ/mol channel against the total observed rate would be an unjustified collapse and is explicitly forbidden for this trail.
Use of the high-pressure limit removes finite-pressure falloff/stabilization mapping from the selected comparator, while parallel entrance-channel structure remains explicit.

preserved_parallel_trail.note: This propene trail is an independent alternative candidate. It does not supersede, relabel, or promote the held ethylene trail.

notes: READY_FOR_ADJUDICATION is not admission and assigns no Barrier Atlas grade.
The Kurylo high-pressure rate is used exactly as an observed total-addition comparator, not as a source from which either theoretical barrier is back-calculated.
The v0.9 workbook and archive hashes remain unchanged.
